text:
jess: quick idea — instead of hard draining reservations when workload drops, what if we do a "soft-reserve taper" that reduces prewarm admission gradually over a configurable window? avoids churn + flapping. open to bikeshedding on names :thinking:

raj: mm, interesting. do you mean we throttle new prewarm admissions rather than tear down existing warm instances?

jess: exactly. keep existing warm slots until their leases expire, but lower the admit rate so we don't spin up more. also add a drift-correction hook to reclaim very stale reserved capacity that isn't used for X minutes.

chen: want to see the config shape. and what's the signal to start tapering? cpu/gpu utilization? inflight request queue?

jess: prototype config below — simple and readable.

```
prewarm:
  mode: taper
  target_headroom_pct: 10        # desired % headroom after taper
  taper_window_s: 300            # how long to ramp down admission
  max_refill_rate: 0.25          # fraction of headroom allowed to refill per minute
  idle_drain_threshold_s: 900    # reclaim reserved slots not used for this long
```

liz: curious about safety: if we ramp down too aggressively and workload spikes, latency suffers. what's the fallback?

jess: plan A: immediate short-circuit to cold-burst fast-path that uses small preemptible pool. plan B: if headroom breaches < 2% and p95 latency rises, temporarily abort taper and force refill.

 taylor: how do we detect "drift" vs real sustained drop? naive idle_drain could kill tenants with infrequent traffic (cron jobs). need tenant-level exceptions or TTLs per reservation.

raj: +1. maybe default to tenant-tagged reservations: ephemeral (low TTL) vs persistent (manual or SLA-backed). persistent reservations ignore idle_drain unless manually revoked.

chen: operator boundary question: should the taper controller live in the operator or in the control-plane autoscaler? my vote: control-plane, because it's global policy-aware and can do cross-tenant smoothing. operator can implement local enforcement only.

jess: I sketched both models. control-plane has better global view (cost fairness), operator is lower-latency to evict. hybrid could work: control-plane computes desired admit_rate + drain hints, operator enforces and reports telemetry.

liz: sounds good. also need audit trail + recommended staging rollout. we don't want silent implicit reclaiming for enterprise customers.

jess: agreed — expose per-tenant policy + events: `taper_started`, `taper_aborted`, `idle_reclaimed`. integrate with console timeline.

raj: testing plan: synthetic traffic with bursty diurnal pattern + random cron noise. measure cold-start count, p95 latency, cost delta. also chaos test preemptible fallback.

chen: edge case: model warmup that takes minutes (big LLMs). Taper must respect `warmup_window` per model and not evict slots still in KV-warmup. add a `protected_until` timestamp on leases.

jess: good call. add `protected_until` and make idle_drain check compare last_active_ts and protected_until.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: update operator RBAC for idle-reclaim, add feature flag `soft_reserve_taper` and telemetry counters: taper_events, idle_reclaims, emergency_refills.

liz: rubric for defaults? for hosted tenants maybe conservative (target_headroom_pct 15, taper_window 600). for Dedicated customers we default off and require opt-in or set via SLA.

raj: SLA behavior is important. Dedicated pools can be configured to preserve reservation invariants. soft taper is useful for shared pools where utilization matters.

taylor: one more thought: admission smoothing math. we should avoid naive linear ramps. use exponential backoff for admit_rate so we adapt faster to drops but back off slower on refills. sketch: admit_rate(t+1)=admit_rate(t)*exp(-dt/tau)+target*(1-exp(-dt/tau)).

jess: love it. I'll prototype admit_rate controller with that equation.

chen: can you also add metrics to detect oscillation? we should track `admit_rate_changes_per_min` and suppress if > threshold.

jess: noted. action items: 
- jess: prototype taper controller + config and publish RFC draft
- taylor + raj: design tests and telemetry
- chen: operator enforcement sketch + RBAC
- liz: draft enterprise opt-in/opt-out UX and console events
- ops-bot: ensure feature-flag gating and required telemetry

jess: will post RFC link when ready. thanks all :+1: :eyes:
